under Sections 498A, 354A, 354C, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, (hereinafter referred to as the 'IPC'), as well as, the proceedings resultant thereto, which are stated to be pending before the Court of learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Court No.1, Solan, H.P. (hereinafter referred to as the 'trial Court').
2.
The relief of quashing has been sought on the basis of the compromise, effected between the parties.

3. According to the petitioner, the marriage of Parvez Khan, son of petitioners No.1 and 2 and brother of petitioner No.3, was solemnized with respondent No.2 and after the marriage, they started residing in a joint family.
Thereafter, some matrimonial dispute has arisen between them and they separated from the petitioners and started residing in a room, adjoining to the residence of the petitioners.
Subsequently, husband of respondent No.2 had gone to Dubai in order to earn livelihood and he used to provide all types of basic necessities to her 4.
It is the further case of the petitioners that due to some temperamental differences, respondent No.2 has lodged the FIR in question against the petitioners and her 3 2024:HHC:14271 husband.

After registration of FIR, the police has investigated the matter and the final report, under Section 173(2) of CrPC, has been submitted, which is pending adjudication, before the learned trial Court.

5. It is the further case of the petitioners that since, Parvez Khan and respondent No.2 were living separately, as such, respondent No.2 had filed the petition, under Section 2 of Muslim Act for dissolution of her marriage, by way of decree of divorce.
The said petition was allowed by the Court of learned Additional Principal Judge- I, Family Court, Solan, H.P., vide judgment dated 15.03.2024.

entities.text: Additional Principal Judge- I, Family Court, Solan, H.P.
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Thereafter, respondent No.2 has performed the second marriage.

6. According to the petitioners, now, the matter has been compromised between them and respondent No.2, vide Compromise Deed Annexure P-3.
7.

On the basis of the said compromise, a prayer has been made to allow the petition, as prayed for,
by quashing the FIR, in question, as well as, proceedings resultant thereto, pending before the learned trial Court.

8. When put to notice, respondent No.1-State has filed the status report, mentioning therein, the 4 2024:HHC:14271 circumstances, in which, the FIR, in question, has been registered, at the instance of respondent No.2, as well as, the manner, in which, the investigation has been conducted, by the police, in this case.
9.

The petitioners have impleaded the complainant, as respondent No.2.
10.

Today, respondent No.2-complainant appeared before the Court and deposed, on oath, that her marriage was solemnized with Parvez Khan on 01.11.2013 and out of the said wedlock, they have been blessed with a daughter.
After some time, due to non-compatibility of temperament, it was not Decided On : 12.12.2024

2 possible for her to live in the matrimonial home with her husband and due to all these facts, she lodged the FIR, in question, against the petitioners.

11. As per further deposition of respondent No.2, she had filed the petition, under Section 2 of the Muslim Marriage Act, 1939 for dissolution of her marriage by way of decree of divorce, before the Court of learned Additional Principal Judge-1, Family Court, Solan, District Solan, H.P.

entities.text: Additional Principal Judge-1, Family Court, Solan, District Solan, H.P.
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The said petition was allowed, vide judgment dated 15.03.2024 (Annexure P-2).
5 2024:HHC:14271 12.

Respondent No.2 has further deposed that her marriage with Parvez Khan has now been dissolved and the matter has been compromised between her and the petitioners, as such, she does not want to proceed further with the FIR, in question.

13. Apart from this, respondent No.2 has also shown her voluntariness and willingness to enter into the compromise with the petitioners, by stating that she has entered into the compromise with the petitioners voluntarily and without any influence from any person.
14. In addition to this, respondent No.2 has made no objection, in case, the present petition is allowed and the FIR, in question, as well as, the resultant proceedings, thereto, are quashed.
15. Today i.e. on 12.12.2024, similar joint statement of petitioners has also been recorded, on oath.

16. Heard.
17.

In this case, the criminal machinery was put into motion, by respondent No.2, by lodging the FIR, in question, against the petitioners, however, when, appeared before this Court, she has exonerated the petitioners from the allegations, as levelled, in this case.

Once, the person, who had put the criminal machinery into motion, has exonerated the petitioners from the allegations, by stating, on oath, that the matter has been compromised between them, in such situation, the chances of success of prosecution case, against the petitioners, are not so bright.

19. When, the parties admittedly have buried all their disputes, by compromising the matter, vide compromise Annexure P-3, then, permitting the proceedings to continue, would be nothing, but,
abuse of the process of law.
20. The primary purpose of law is to maintain peace and harmony in the society.
Acceptance of the petition would also give another opportunity to the petitioners, as well as, respondent No.2 to live peacefully in the society.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even otherwise, acceptance of the compromise, by this Court, will save the precious judicial time of the learned trial Court, which, the learned trial Court will be in a position to devote for the decision of some other serious matters, pending before it.
Moreover, this Court is 7 2024:HHC:14271 satisfied with the genuineness of the compromise Annexure P-3, entered into between the parties.

22. Considering all these facts, the petition is allowed and FIR No.12 of 2019, dated 11.04.2019,
registered with Women Police Station, Solan, H.P., under Sections 498A, 354A, 354C, 506 and 34 of the IPC, as well as, the proceedings resultant thereto, pending before the learned trial Court, against the petitioners, are ordered to be quashed.
23. The compromise deed, Annexure P-3, and the statements of the parties, recorded today in the Court, shall form part of the judgment.
24. Pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of accordingly.
( Virender Singh ) Judge December 12, 2024 (Gaurav Thakur)
